messages.subject: Define sampless CIMP status?
messages.body_plain:
I want to use methylKit to define the CIMP status of my samples. My understanding is that samples can be considered CIMP-high is they exhibit 10% methylation or higher in the following genes' promoters: RUNX3, CACNA1G, IGF2, MLH1, NEUROG1, SOCS1, CDKN2A.

What I am not clear on, is how I can define regions that correspond to these gene's promoters in order to use the percMethyatlion() command?

Are there annotations already included in methylKit that I can use to define my samples' CIMP status? If I need to load annotation data that I acquire from somewhere else, what is the simplest and most straightforward way to do so?

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Define sampless CIMP status?
messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure how exactly original CIMP classification works, it was probably based on 450k arrays or some other array setup. Assuming your understanding is correct.

You can extract promoter regions of transcripts using readTranscriptFeatures() and use regionCounts() to summarize methylation info on promoter regions of your genes. You first need to filter the genes you are interested in either by supplying a bed file that only contains your genes of interest or filtering within R by using gene ids.

Then you can use percMethylation() on the resulting object from regionCounts() if the object is methylBase object. If not, you can either use unite() then percMethylation or if the objects are methylRaw objects you can simply divide numCs column by coverage column of the methyRaw objects to get methylation ratio per promoter of interest.

Best,
Altuna

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am having my own peculiar problems trying to install methylKit, on OS X 10.7.5.  When I open R and follow the install instruction from GitHub, this is what I get:

> library(devtools)
Warning message:
package ‘devtools’ was built under R version 3.2.5
> install_github("al2na/methylKit", build_vignettes=FALSE,
+   repos=BiocInstaller::biocinstallRepos(),
+   dependencies=TRUE)
Downloading GitHub repo al2na/methylKit@master
from URL https://api.github.com/repos/al2na/methylKit/zipball/master
Installing methylKit
trying URL 'http://probability.ca/cran/bin/macosx/contrib/3.2/emdbook_1.3.9'
Error in download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) :
  cannot open URL 'http://probability.ca/cran/bin/macosx/contrib/3.2/emdbook_1.3.9'
In addition: Warning message:
In download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) :
  cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'
Warning in download.packages(x$name, destdir = dest_dir, repos = x$repos,  :
  download of package ‘emdbook’ failed
Error in download.packages(x$name, destdir = dest_dir, repos = x$repos,  :
  subscript out of bounds

I get the same message when adding type="source".

If I try the above with dependencies=F, I get:

> install_github("al2na/methylKit", build_vignettes=FALSE,
+   repos=BiocInstaller::biocinstallRepos(),
+   dependencies=F)
Downloading GitHub repo al2na/methylKit@master
from URL https://api.github.com/repos/al2na/methylKit/zipball/master
Installing methylKit
'/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R' --no-site-file --no-environ --no-save --no-restore --quiet CMD INSTALL  \
  '/private/var/folders/pd/3vkzqgqs6qn4405507d5ryjc0000gn/T/Rtmpy7jj9M/devtoolsb26276eab50a/al2na-methylKit-a9f1f93' --library='/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.2/Resources/library' --install-tests

ERROR: this R is version 3.2.1, package 'methylKit' requires R >= 3.3.0
Error: Command failed (1)

Since I have OS X 10.7.5, I am not able to install R version 3.3.1 which is only for >= OS X 10.9 ; instead, I have to install R 3.2.1 as shown on https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/

Lastly, when I try to execute R CMD INSTALL methylKit_0.9.2.tar.gz from the terminal I get the following:

* installing to library ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.2/Resources/library’
* installing *source* package ‘methylKit’ ...
** R
** data
** exec
** inst
** preparing package for lazy loading
Error : objects ‘DataFrame’, ‘Rle’, ‘elementMetadata’, ‘elementMetadata<-’ are not exported by 'namespace:IRanges'
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package ‘methylKit’
* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.2/Resources/library/methylKit’

I get exactly the same message even when trying R CMD INSTALL methylKit_0.5.7.tar.gz

The BioConductor version I'm using is 3.2 but it seems that 3.3 will only work with version >= 3.3.0.

I would greatly appreciate any help for this issue.  Please let me know if you need more info.

Thank you,
Rajat

messages.subject: using adjustMethylC()
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to understand how adjustMethylC() works because I am afraid I may be misunderstanding the documentation. To avoid any confusion regarding nomenclature and to make the question more generic, I am not referring to anything as 5mC/5hmC. Let's say, I call adjustMethylC(X, Y). Does that mean it will simply return the difference in methylation levels at each site between X and Y (X-Y)?

How does it deal with different coverage levels? If a site is covered in X, but not Y, what is the difference? Is it X-0 or not returned?

What if Y is greater than X? Will the returned difference be 0 or negative or an error?

On Fri, Jul 8, 2016 at 9:56 PM, <dolg...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I am trying to understand how adjustMethylC() works because I am afraid I may be misunderstanding the documentation. To avoid any confusion regarding nomenclature and to make the question more generic, I am not referring to anything as 5mC/5hmC. Let's say, I call adjustMethylC(X, Y). Does that mean it will simply return the difference in methylation levels at each site between X and Y (X-Y)?
>

It will return the adjusted methylated and unmethylated C counts by using the percentage of methylated Cs in Y.

> How does it deal with different coverage levels? If a site is covered in X, but not Y, what is the difference? Is it X-0 or not returned?
>

The site has to be covered in both cases, if it is not the base is discarded.

> What if Y is greater than X? Will the returned difference be 0 or negative or an error?
>

if Y is greater than X, X is set to 0.

Best,
Altuna

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've generated a methylDiff object that displays the DMR locations for my sample set. Right now, I'm trying to annotate the methylDiff object with regulatory information (ORegAnno sites) and obtain a list of the DMR locations that overlap with these regulatory sites. I used the UCSC Table Browser to download a BedGraph for the regulatory information and was able to use readBed to generate a corresponding GRanges object that contains the ranges of these regulatory features.

I've used annotateWithFeature to annotate my methylDiff object, but right now all I can see is the overall percentage of my target features that overlap with the annotation, not the genomic coordinates themselves. Is there a method to obtain the full list of genomic locations/corresponding regulatory IDs that were annotated?

I tried using the selectByOverlap function mentioned in the documentation to select rows from the methylDiff object that lay within the ranges of the regulatory GRanges object, but when I tried to run it it gave me the message

Error in selecByOverlap(methylDiff, Granges object) :
no slot of name “subjectHits” for this object of class “SortedByQueryHits”

Extending that further, is there a way to view the full list of genomic coordinates contained within a methylDiff object and see if they overlap with promoters/introns etc.? I've used getAssociationWithTSS, but I'd like to get a list of my DMRs in terms of which ones lie within promoters/introns/exons/intergenic rather than their distance from the TSS.

messages.body_plain:
I have been comparing methylation in a set of samples by focusing on a subset of genomic regions listed in a BED file (they are probes from Illumina's 450K DNA methylation bead chip). Once I have read in my methylation call files, filtered and normalized my methylRawList into an object called filt_obj my code goes like this:

ill_45.obj = readBed("~/Illumina/hg19_450K.bed")
probe_counts <- regionCounts(filt_obj, ill_45.obj)
uni_probes = unite(probe_counts)
perc_meth = percMethylation(uni_probes, rowids = TRUE)
# COMPUTE STANDARD DEVIATIONS TO GET 5% MOST VARIANT LOCI
std_devs = rowSds(perc_meth, na.rm = TRUE)
cutoff = quantile(std_devs, 0.95)
top_05 = subset(perc_meth, std_devs > cutoff)
pheatmap(top_05)

I want to remove from consideration those regions of the genome that show high methylation in my normal samples. I figure I can do this by simply choosing a cut-off value and subsetting the table I created with my percMethylation() command but I wondered if there is a better way to do this using methylKit commands?

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Urgent: min.per.group for multiple groups
messages.body_plain:
The current functionality (based on the source code here <https://github.com/al2na/methylKit/blob/master/R/backbone.R> , about halfway down) expects a single integer to be used for both groups, so it won't quite do what you want. One quasi-solution would be to use the reorganize function to temporarily assign the samples to a single group, to at least ensure coverage over most of the data.

If you really want to try with unequal groups and need it quickly, you can try copying the code and making your own custom version of the unite function by tweaking this section to make min.per.group a vector and indexing into it:

for(i in unique(object@treatment) ){
my.ind=coverage.ind[object@treatment==i]
ldat = !is.na <http://is.na>(df[,my.ind,with=FALSE])
if( is.null(dim(ldat)) ){ # if there is only one dimension
df=df[ldat>=min.per.group,]
}else{
df=df[rowSums(ldat)>=min.per.group,]
}
}
